At forty-one thousand feet, both engines of this brand new jet went silent. The fuel tanks were completely empty. The fuel gauge was broken, so the crew did the math by hand. But this jet measured fuel in kilograms, not pounds. Mixing them up, the crew loaded less than half the fuel they needed. Halfway to Edmonton, the jet ran dry. Luckily, Captain Bob Pearson was also a glider pilot. He flew the silent jet for seventeen minutes, looking for a runway. His co-pilot knew an old air base at Gimli, now a racetrack. All sixty-nine survived, and the jet got a nickname: the Gimli Glider.
